title: Share of the Surplus Moved from Accounts That Money Leaves Often
content:
Only part of the surplus moves out of an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts where money leaves the account often. Two facts decide the share: the count of withdrawals posted to the account in the three calendar months ending on the instruction date, and the whole months the account has been open.

- **3 or more withdrawals in that window, and the account open no more than 36 whole months** — three quarters of the surplus is moved, that is 0.75 of it.
- **Exactly 2 withdrawals in that window, and the account open no more than 36 whole months** — nine tenths of the surplus is moved, that is 0.90 of it.
- **Fewer than 2 withdrawals in that window, or the account open more than 36 whole months** — the whole surplus is moved, that is 1 times it.

### The three shares on one surplus

Take a hypothetical surplus of 8000.00 USD. Three quarters of it is 6000.00 USD, nine tenths is 7200.00 USD, and the whole of it is 8000.00 USD.

### Both conditions bind

An account open 50 whole months moves the whole surplus however many withdrawals posted in the window, and an account open 6 whole months with a single withdrawal in the window moves the whole surplus likewise.

An account open exactly 36 whole months still satisfies the age condition; one open 37 whole months does not. A count of exactly 3 withdrawals gives three quarters and a count of exactly 2 gives nine tenths.
